subtitle: The Regent Who Barred the Western Gate

panels.shot: epic low-angle wide of Naikidevi on a fort wall, desert and distant army faint on the horizon
panels.action: Naikidevi stands firm on the ramparts of Patan, veil stirred by hot desert wind, hands resting on the parapet as the distant blur of a marching host glimmers beyond the Thar.

dialogue.text: In 1178, as Muhammad of Ghor drove toward Gujarat, a widowed regent named Naikidevi chose the ground where his road would end.

i18n.hi: ११७८ में, जब मोहम्मद ग़ोरी गुजरात की ओर बढ़ा, विधवा रीजेंट नैकिदेवी ने वही जगह चुनी जहाँ उसका रास्ता खत्म होना था।

panels.shot: slow push-in from cityscape of Patan to throne hall interior
panels.action: A wide view of bustling Patan with its stepped wells and temples fades inward to Naikidevi seated on the Chaulukya throne, a child’s empty throne beside her, ministers and feudatory envoys in attendance.

dialogue.text: Patan, capital of the Chaulukyas of Gujarat. King Ajayapala dead, his son Mularaja a child, the kingdom held together by one word on every grant and order: ‘Naikidevi, regent.’

i18n.hi: पाटन, गुजरात के चालुक्यों की राजधानी। राजा अजयराज मरे, बेटा मूलराज़ नाबालिग, और हर फ़रमान पर एक ही शब्द राज चला रहा था: ‘रीजेंट नैकिदेवी।’

panels.shot: tight mid-shot of Naikidevi at a council, angled from slightly below
panels.action: Naikidevi leans forward over a low council table strewn with palm-leaf documents and a rough map of western India, her face calm but intent as a messenger kneels, dust-streaked, before her.

dialogue.speaker: Messenger
dialogue.text: Devi, word from the north: a Turushka army has crossed the passes.

i18n.hi: देवी, उत्तर से खबर है: तुरुष्कों की सेना दर्रे पार कर चुकी है।

panels.shot: over-the-shoulder view from behind Naikidevi toward the map on the floor
panels.action: Seen from behind Naikidevi’s shoulder, a hand points on the map from Ghazni across the Sindhu and down the Thar, tracing a line toward Nahrwala, while courtiers watch in uneasy silence.

dialogue.text: In distant Ghur, the Shansabani prince Muhammad had turned from Ghor to Ghazni, from Kabul to the plains. Now his men, the Tabaqat-i-Nasiri says, marched toward Nahrwala in Gujarat.

i18n.hi: दूर घूर में शंसबानी राजकुमार मोहम्मद घूर से ग़ज़नी, काबुल से मैदानों की ओर मुड़ चुका था। अब, तबकात-ए-नासिरी कहता है, उसकी फौज गुजरात के नहरवाला की तरफ़ बढ़ी।

panels.shot: cut to a harsh landscape wide of the Thar route, caravan and riders in the distance
panels.action: A long, heat-hazed view of camel caravans and armoured riders moving along a sandy track, dunes and thorn scrub on either side, with a distant glimmer of a mosque-topped fort on the horizon.

dialogue.text: The Kiradu inscription had already spoken of Turushka attacks, of temples damaged, of repairs that followed. Now a larger host advanced, not for a raid, but for the rich fields of Gujarat.

i18n.hi: किराडू के शिलालेख में पहले ही तुरुष्क हमलों, टूटे मंदिरों और फिर हुई मरम्मत का ज़िक्र था। अब बड़ी सेना चली, लूट के लिए नहीं, गुजरात की समृद्ध ज़मीनों के लिए।

panels.shot: intimate close-up on Naikidevi’s eyes, lit by lamplight
panels.action: In the glow of an oil lamp, Naikidevi’s eyes narrow in thought, the faint reflection of a tiny temple tower in her pupils as the murmur of the court fades to a hush around her.

dialogue.text: Later storytellers would picture her riding into battle with her child in her lap. The chronicles are quieter. They simply show a regent who held authority, and a decision she would not delay.

i18n.hi: बाद के किस्सों में उसे गोद में बच्चे को लेकर घोड़े पर युद्ध में जाते दिखाया गया। इतिहास-ग्रंथ चुप हैं। वे बस एक रीजेंट दिखाते हैं जिसके हाथ में सत्ता थी, और जो निर्णय टालती नहीं थी।

panels.shot: medium wide of court scene as she addresses feudatories, slightly elevated angle
panels.action: Naikidevi rises from the throne, one hand raised toward a row of seated feudatory chiefs with distinct crests and attire, their faces a mix of pride and concern.

dialogue.speaker: Naikidevi
dialogue.text: If we wait behind walls, we yield the roads. We will choose our ground.

i18n.hi: अगर हम दीवारों के पीछे छिपे रहे, तो सड़कें छोड़ देंगे। ज़मीन हम चुनेंगे।

panels.shot: montage-style wide showing different chiefs in their own domains receiving summons
panels.action: A split-scene panel: Kirtipala at Jalor reading a royal order, Kelhanadeva near the rocky hills of Nadol consulting his captains, Dharavarsha in his court, each framed against their own banners as riders depart.

dialogue.text: Inscriptions on Sundha Hill would later carve their names: Kirtipala, Kelhanadeva, Dharavarsha. The regent’s summons called not for a single champion, but for a coalition.

i18n.hi: सुंधा पहाड़ी के लेख में बाद में नाम उभरे: कीर्तिपाल, केलेहनदेव, धरवर्ष। रीजेंट ने किसी अकेले वीर को नहीं, एक संगठित मोर्चे को बुलाया।

panels.shot: broad landscape shot of the Aravalli foothills near Mount Abu, early morning light
panels.action: The rugged foothills near Mount Abu rise under a pale dawn, narrow passes twisting between rocks and scrub; a small Chaulukya war council stands on a ridge, looking down to the plain below.

dialogue.text: Near Mount Abu, at Kasahrada, the land itself offered a weapon: tight passes, broken ground, flanks of stone. Here, Naikidevi’s coalition would meet the Ghurid road.

i18n.hi: माउंट आबू के पास, कषहराड़ा में, धरती ने खुद हथियार दिया: तंग दर्रे, टूटी ज़मीन, पत्थरों की ढाल। यहीं नैकिदेवी का गठबंधन घुरी रास्ते से टकराएगा।

panels.shot: mid-shot of Naikidevi in a campaign pavilion, conferring with generals with map between them
panels.action: Inside a campaign pavilion, Naikidevi stands beside seasoned generals, fingers resting on a drawn plan of the pass as armoured horsemen wait outside; her face is resolute yet composed.

dialogue.text: The Sundha inscription will praise the warriors who broke the Turushkas. The Tabaqat will recall a disastrous march. Between them we see her work: the choice of ground, the placing of men.

i18n.hi: सुंधा लेख उन वीरों की खूब तारीफ़ करेगा जिन्होंने तुरुष्कों को तोड़ा। तबकात इस सफ़र को विनाशकारी मार्च कहेगा। दोनों के बीच में नज़र आता है उसका काम: ज़मीन चुनना, सेनाएँ जमाना।

panels.shot: wide establishing shot of the Ghurid vanguard entering the constricted pass
panels.action: Armoured Ghurid cavalry and standard-bearers wind into a narrow valley, their column stretching back into the haze; rocky slopes press close, and a few loose stones lie freshly dislodged above them.

dialogue.text: The Ghurid host, hardened by marches from the Oxus to the Indus, moved into the Kasahrada defile. To them, Gujarat promised plunder and passage to the sea.

i18n.hi: ऑक्सस से सिंधु तक के लंबे मार्चों से सख़्त हुई घुरी सेना कषहराड़ा की घाटी में उतरी। उनके लिए गुजरात लूट और समंदर की राह का वादा था।

panels.shot: dynamic high-angle shot from cliffside, Chaulukya and Rajput forces poised to descend
panels.action: From a crag above, Chaulukya and allied Rajput horsemen wait poised at the edge, lances ready, archers already loosing arrows down into the valley as dust begins to rise from below.

dialogue.text: But on the heights, Gujarat and its allies had already arrived. Later verses would boast of elephants and steeds surging downhill, of the Turushka line thrown into confusion.

i18n.hi: लेकिन ऊँचाइयों पर गुजरात और उसके साथी पहले ही पहुँच चुके थे। बाद के छंद हाथियों और घोड़ों के ढलानों से टूट पड़ने, और तुरुष्क पंक्ति के बिखरने के गीत गाएंगे।

panels.shot: cinematic wide of chaotic battlefield at the foothills, dust and motion without gore
panels.action: A broad view of the battlefield at the foothills shows war elephants pressing into disordered cavalry, riders wheeling away, standards fallen into the dust, all under a cloud of churned earth and sunlight.

dialogue.text: The Tabaqat-i-Nasiri does not linger on detail. It records that the army marching toward Nahrwala was routed, its commander escaping with difficulty, its ranks scattered by defeat.

i18n.hi: तबकात-ए-नासिरी ठहर कर विवरण नहीं देता। बस लिखता है कि नहरवाला की ओर बढ़ती फौज टूटकर भागी, सेनापति जान बचाकर निकला, और पंक्तियाँ हार से बिखर गईं।

panels.shot: contrasting calm shot of Naikidevi in a field tent receiving news, medium close
panels.action: In a simple field tent away from the fighting, Naikidevi stands as a breathless rider kneels, offering a folded message; outside, exhausted soldiers rest against their shields.

dialogue.speaker: Messenger
dialogue.text: Devi, the Turushka host is broken. Their prince has fled the field.

i18n.hi: देवी, तुरुष्कों की फ़ौज चकनाचूर हो गई। उनका शाहज़ादा मैदान छोड़ भाग निकला।

panels.shot: profile close-up of Naikidevi, expression controlled, with faint relief
panels.action: In profile, Naikidevi closes her eyes briefly, exhaling, then looks toward the distant hills with a composed, almost stern calm, fingers tightening lightly on the edge of a wooden table.

dialogue.text: No chronicler records her words in that moment. Yet every inscription that follows speaks of what her decision secured: the young king’s throne, the western gate, the fragile balance of power.

i18n.hi: उस पल उसके शब्द किसी इतिहासकार ने नहीं लिखे। पर हर अगला शिलालेख कहता है कि उसके निर्णय ने क्या बचाया: नन्हे राजा का सिंहासन, पश्चिम का दरवाज़ा, ताक़त का नाज़ुक संतुलन।

panels.shot: wide shot of a temple town being repaired, artisans at work, Naikidevi visiting
panels.action: In a temple town, scaffolds rise as artisans reset carved stones and repaint faded images; Naikidevi watches quietly from a shaded pavilion, priests and townsfolk gathered respectfully behind her.

dialogue.text: The Kiradu record had spoken of temples harmed in earlier Turushka raids and later repaired. Victories like Kasahrada did not end that cycle, but they gave space to rebuild between storms.

i18n.hi: किराडू के लेख में पहले के तुरुष्क हमलों में टूटे मंदिरों और बाद में हुई मरम्मत का ज़िक्र था। कषहराड़ा जैसी जीतों ने उस चक्र को ख़त्म नहीं किया, पर तूफ़ानों के बीच मरम्मत की मोहलत दी।

panels.shot: time-lapse style composition showing later scribes carving the Sundha Hill inscription
panels.action: Stonecutters on Sundha Hill chisel lines into a rock face, a Brahmin scholar dictating nearby; in a faint overlay, Naikidevi is seen years earlier, seated in court, as if remembered in their words.

dialogue.text: On Sundha Hill, the Jalor Chahamanas carved their boast: how they helped break the Turushka host at Kasahrada. Behind their pride stands the regent who made their gathering possible.

i18n.hi: सुंधा पहाड़ी पर जालौर के चाहमानों ने डींग हाँकी: कैसे उन्होंने कषहराड़ा में तुरुष्क सेना तोड़ने में हाथ बँटाया। उनकी शान के पीछे वही रीजेंट है जिसने यह जुटान संभव की।

panels.shot: somber interior shot of Patan court years later, Naikidevi older, with grown Mularaja beside
panels.action: Years later in the Patan hall, an older Naikidevi stands slightly behind a now-grown Mularaja on the throne, her posture relaxed yet alert as envoys from distant lands bow before the court.

dialogue.text: The Ghurids would return to Gujarat under Qutb al-Din Aibak in 1197, and this time they would succeed. Their first attempt, though, had already been blunted by a regent’s choice of field.

i18n.hi: घूरी फिर ११९७ में क़ुतुबुद्दीन ऐबक के साथ गुजरात लौटे, और इस बार जीत गए। लेकिन उनकी पहली चढ़ाई को पहले ही एक रीजेंट के चुने मैदान ने कुंद कर दिया था।

panels.shot: final reflective wide shot of the Thar route and Aravalli hills at sunset, Naikidevi’s silhouette faintly superimposed
panels.action: The sun sets over the Thar route and the Aravalli line near Mount Abu, tracks fading into the sand; faintly, like a memory, Naikidevi’s silhouette looks on from the sky’s edge.

dialogue.text: Her name survives in grants and inscriptions, not epics, yet in 1178 Naikidevi showed how power can be held: by seeing the storm early, and choosing the ground before the battle begins.

i18n.hi: उसका नाम दानपत्रों और शिलालेखों में बचा, महाकाव्यों में नहीं। पर ११७८ में नैकिदेवी ने दिखा दिया कि सत्ता कैसे थामी जाती है: तूफ़ान को पहले पहचानकर, और जंग से पहले ही ज़मीन चुनकर।

subtitle_i18n.en: The Regent Who Barred the Western Gate
subtitle_i18n.hi: जिस रीजेंट ने पश्चिमी फाटक बंद किया
